clinician.final_diagnosis: Angiolymphoid hyperplasia with eosinophilia (ALHE) with concurrent scalp demodicosis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 25-year-old female presented to a dermatology clinic in Rustaq, Oman in 2021 with a 6-month history of itchy, pearly papules on her scalp. Clinical examination revealed multiple grouped erythematous papules and nodules (average 1 cm diameter) on the left temporo-occipital region, with secondary ulcerations and bleeding from scratching. Systemic examination was unremarkable without lymphadenopathy. Comprehensive laboratory workup including CBC (with normal eosinophils), renal function, serum IgE, HIV screening, and urinalysis were all normal. A scalp biopsy was performed, which revealed histopathologic features diagnostic of ALHE: variable-sized blood vessels lined by plump histiocytoid endothelial cells with inflammatory infiltrates comprising lymphocytes and eosinophils in the dermis. The same biopsy specimen also demonstrated Demodex mite infestation in the sebaceous ducts, confirming concurrent demodicosis. The patient was treated with 10 sessions of cryotherapy (2 freeze-thaw cycles per week per lesion) combined with twice-daily topical metronidazole gel application. The patient showed remarkable clinical improvement within 7 weeks of treatment.

Histopathologic confirmation of demodicosis: Demodex mite infestation in sebaceous ducts
